scenario: A railway authority files formal reports only for delays exceeding 60 minutes. Among filed reports the mean delay is 95 minutes (σ=20 min). Policy analysts need the true mean delay across all delayed freight movements.

data.description: Observed statistics among units exceeding reporting threshold

values.n_observed: only values above threshold are recorded

question: (a) Assuming the true distribution of delay duration is normal with σ=20 minutes, solve for the true population mean μ such that E[X|X>60]=95. (b) What fraction of all events lie above the above 60-minute incident-report threshold threshold? (c) By how much does the observed mean overstate the true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: Solving the truncated-normal equation μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 95 numerically gives μ≈92.8126. Only 95.0% of all events are actually observed; the observed mean overstates the true mean by ≈2.1874 minutes.

naive_answer: The true mean delay duration is approximately 95 minutes because that is what the data directly show.
naive_trap: The observed mean is a truncated-normal conditional expectation, not the population mean; it always exceeds the true mean for above-threshold samples.
reasoning_trace: (1) Let α=(t−μ)/σ. (2) E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 95 and solve numerically for μ using brentq. (4) Solution: μ≈92.8126. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((60−92.8126)/σ)≈0.94956.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 95,20,60
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-92.8126)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.94956)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
